questions.question: When coupling, you should:

options.text: Connect the correct glad hands together.
Connect only one set of glad hands.
Leave one glad hand disconnected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the correct glad hands together.
questions.explanation: When coupling air brake hoses, connect the correct glad hands to each other. They are often color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is typically for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: An empty combination vehicle has stiff suspension springs and strong brakes. These will have:

options.text: High traction.
Low traction.
No traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low traction.
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle stops more slowly than a loaded one. With less weight in the trailer, the stiff suspension springs and strong brakes have lower traction than they would with more weight.

questions.question: Rearward amplification refers to:

options.text: The amount of noise coming from the rear of the vehicle.
The cause of the "crack-the-whip" effect.
The number of trailers a tractor can pull.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cause of the "crack-the-whip" effect.
questions.explanation: Rearward amplification causes the "crack-the-whip" effect. If not handled properly, a trailer can tip over because of rearward amplification.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows a vehicle's wheels to lock up.
It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
It makes turning a vehicle easier.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheel lockup during hard braking. If ABS detects that wheels are about to lock, it reduces brake pressure to a safe level.

questions.question: If the emergency air line loses pressure:

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System will activate.
The service air line will activate.
The emergency brakes will activate.

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency brakes will activate.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes on a combination vehicle. If the emergency line loses air pressure, the emergency trailer brakes will activate.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer:

options.text: Connect the correct glad hands together.
Any glad hands can be connected to each other.
Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the correct glad hands together.
questions.explanation: When coupling, connect matching glad hands. They are often color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is typically for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away:

options.text: The trailer will stop normally.
The trailer will have no brakes.
The trailer will speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away from an older trailer's air tank, the trailer will have no working brakes and the wheels will turn freely.

questions.question: A combination vehicle has ____ air line(s).

options.text: One
Two
Three

questions.correctAnswerText: Two
questions.explanation: Every combination vehicle has two air lines: the service line and the emergency line.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, you must turn the steering wheel:

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to move.
In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to move.
To the left until backing is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to move.
questions.explanation: When backing a vehicle with a trailer, turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the steering wheel the other way to follow the trailer.

questions.question: The ____ trailer is most likely to tip over if a driver turns too quickly.

options.text: Front
Last
Middle

questions.correctAnswerText: Last
questions.explanation: When turning, steer gently and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous and can cause the last trailer to roll over.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand brake while your trailer is skidding?

options.text: It will stop the skid.
It will straighten the trailer.
It will continue the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will continue the skid.
questions.explanation: Using the trailer hand brake while skidding will make the skid worse. Release the brakes instead to help your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: What is true about combination vehicles?

options.text: They often have taller trailers than single commercial vehicles.
They are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
They require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more skill to drive. They are longer, heavier, and easier to roll over than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: What happens if a load is placed on one side of a trailer?

options.text: The trailer may lean during turns.
The trailer may have extra support during turns.
The trailer may be easier to steer during turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer may lean during turns.
questions.explanation: Putting the load on one side makes the trailer lean that way. This increases the risk of rollover when turning or changing lanes.

questions.question: Combination vehicles are usually:

options.text: Easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Lighter than single commercial vehicles.
More difficult to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more skill to drive. They are longer, heavier, and easier to roll over than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: Only when the trailer is carrying a load.
Only to test the trailer's brakes.
Only in bad weather when the trailer may skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer's brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) tests the trailer brakes. Use it only to test brakes. Using it while moving can cause a skid.

questions.question: When should you look into the back of the fifth wheel?

options.text: While testing your air brakes.
If your vehicle begins to skid.
When inspecting a coupling.

questions.correctAnswerText: When inspecting a coupling.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Check that the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: Are fully-loaded rigs more or less likely to roll over?

options.text: They are less likely to roll over than empty rigs.
They are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
They are just as likely to roll over as empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs are more likely to roll over because the heavy cargo raises the center of gravity.

questions.question: After completing a pre-trip inspection, what should you ensure?

options.text: The service line valve is closed.
The trailer hand brake is applied.
The emergency line valve is open.

questions.correctAnswerText: The service line valve is closed.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves and listen for air. Then close both shut-off valves before you start driving.

questions.question: What do shut-off valves do?

options.text: Prevent air from escaping air brake systems.
Prevent air from entering air brake systems.
Control vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent air from escaping air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flowing from one trailer to another. Keep the rear shut-off valve closed to stop air from leaving the brake system.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, how should you press the brake pedal?

options.text: Press it harder than usual.
Press it the same as you normally would.
Press it more lightly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press it the same as you normally would.
questions.explanation: With ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System), brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
